rfp_name: Scaling AI Safety for a Multi-Agent World

tiers.tier1: Up to $300,000 (1-2 years) — exploratory, pilot, focused investigation

S1.name: Sandboxes and Testbeds
S1.description: Realistic, reproducible multi-agent environments for studying frontier-model agent populations. Must be scalable, high-fidelity (frontier models not toy abstractions), externally valid, safe for studying dangerous behaviours, and reproducible.
S1.scoring_question: Does this researcher study, build, or contribute to realistic multi-agent testbeds or simulation environments for frontier AI agents? Consider: agent frameworks, benchmark design, simulation infrastructure, distilled proxy agents, external validity methods, or environment-agnostic logging tools.

S2.name: The Science of Agent Networks
S2.description: System-level safety science of agent populations: how individual properties create population-level outcomes, vulnerability evaluation (cascading failures, adversarial sub-populations), emergent communication, collective agency, and phase transitions.
S2.scoring_question: Does this researcher study the system-level properties of multi-agent populations? Consider: game theory, mechanism design, emergent collective behaviors, multi-agent RL, cascading failures, collective agency, agent network analysis, or theoretical foundations of distributed AI systems.

S3.name: Strengthening Agent Infrastructure
S3.description: Stress-testing and strengthening agent protocols (A2A etc.) for identity, authentication, reputation, accountability, provenance, commitment, and verifiable attributes. Addresses AI-agent-specific challenges: clonability, no persistent biological identity, machine-speed interactions.
S3.scoring_question: Does this researcher work on agent identity, authentication, reputation systems, cryptographic commitments, verifiable attributes, provenance, or accountability for AI agents? Consider: zero-knowledge proofs, cryptographic protocols, formal verification of distributed protocols, Sybil resistance, agent delegation, watermarking, proof-of-inference.

S4.name: Multi-Agent Oversight and Control
S4.description: Detection, attribution, and control of unsafe behaviour in deployed multi-agent systems at scale. Includes collusion detection, steganography detection, circuit breakers, mechanism/information design, scalable oversight, red/blue-team evaluations.
S4.scoring_question: Does this researcher work on monitoring, detecting, attributing, or controlling unsafe behaviours in multi-agent systems? Consider: collusion detection, steganography/covert communication detection, attribution tools, oversight interfaces, AI control methods extended to multi-agent, circuit breakers, red-teaming of agent collectives.

SC1.name: Research Agenda Fit
SC1.description: Does the proposal clearly engage with the intention behind the scientific questions in the research agenda?
SC1.scoring_question: How well does this researcher's existing work and trajectory fit the core agenda of multi-agent AI safety (NOT individual agent alignment, NOT capability advancement, NOT AI for human cooperation)?

SC2.name: Scientific Quality and Rigour
SC2.description: Is the proposed work technically sound, well-motivated, and capable of producing generalisable insight?
SC2.scoring_question: Based on their publication record, methodology, and research depth — how rigorous and technically sound is their work? Consider venue quality, methodological sophistication, and depth of contribution.

SC3.name: Potential Impact
SC3.description: Would the project materially advance scientific understanding or meaningfully improve ability to understand, evaluate, or control risks from multi-principal, multi-agent AI?
SC3.scoring_question: If this researcher applied their skills to the MAAS agenda, how high is the potential for their work to produce generalisable insights that materially advance multi-agent AI safety science?

SC4.name: Philanthropic Fit
SC4.description: Is there a clear market, coordination, or incentive failure that means commercial interests are unlikely to solve this problem?
SC4.scoring_question: Does this researcher work on problems that commercial AI labs (Google, OpenAI, Anthropic) are unlikely to fund or prioritise — foundational, precompetitive, or public-good research on multi-agent safety?

SC5.name: Feasibility and Scope
SC5.description: Is there sufficient evidence that the researcher can execute ambitious but achievable work within 1-2 years?
SC5.scoring_question: Does their track record (prior projects, deliverables, publications) suggest they can execute a focused 1-2 year MAAS research project with concrete outputs?

SC6.name: Team Expertise
SC6.description: Is the team well-suited to execute the proposed work with relevant technical expertise and sufficient capacity?
SC6.scoring_question: How well does this researcher's specific technical background (MAS, game theory, cryptography, distributed systems, AI safety, network science) match what the MAAS agenda actually requires?

SC7.name: Cost Appropriateness
SC7.description: Is the proposed budget reasonable and well-justified given the project's goals and planned activities?
SC7.scoring_question: Based on their institution type, research style, and project scale — would their work likely be scoped to a reasonable budget (Tier 1: up to $300K or Tier 2: up to $1M) with justifiable costs?

out_of_scope_signals: single-agent interpretability with no multi-agent extension
individual model robustness without system-level evaluation
AI for human cooperation (democratic institutions, mediation)
toy game theory without frontier model extension
